reviewer: native DSH subagent, non-author; the same reviewer that measured the defect at cc2e4cc018
headline: The prune repair is real and the adopted probe still bites: reproducing the shipped bug reddens 2 of its 10, and each of the two re-written assertions fails again if the defect it guards returns. One claim in the commit is not in the code: `no_tests` is NOT stated in the node summary line.

evidence: My UNTOUCHED original probe (sha256 2ef2648e9da2af3bb3cb47e159d4e75a6d0d212294d5bbd4d036ce9825621fb1, the file I committed at the last review) run against c4cedca0ee: 8 passed, 2 failed - and both failures are the two assertions that described the old defect. Its prune witness `test_PROBE_multiproject_prune_follows_the_check_that_ran` now PASSES: seed node:web:test red through run_tests, re-run with web's test green, and the baseline file on disk is [] (not ['node:web:test']).

The same run reports the repaired tokens, observed only (no logic replaced): node_ran == ['integrations/dsh:install', 'web:build', 'web:install', 'web:test'] and asked == [('node:web:test', True)]. The baseline is now asked for a key whose pair it holds.

The install-failure half still holds, now for the right reason: web's `ci --offline` exits 1, web's checks == {install}, build/test never launched (asserted from the recorded call list), the baseline keeps ['node:web:test'] and baseline_kept_unproven == ['node:web:test']. Before this commit that also held, but only because nothing ever pruned.

Adopted file tests/unit/test_node_gate_measured_semantics.py + tests/unit/test_run_tests_node_multi_project.py: 23 passed. Broader: 117 passed over the adopted file plus test_run_tests_known_red_baseline.py, test_run_tests_baseline_wiring.py, test_run_tests_gate.py, test_node_gate_executor_boundary.py.

no_tests.install_failure_run: corrected. On a run where web's install FAILED and integrations/dsh (no scripts) passed its install: report['node']['no_tests'] == ['integrations/dsh'] - the broken project is no longer named, the passing script-less project still is, and its install still appears in checks. My untouched probe's old assertion `['web','integrations/dsh']` is exactly what now fails (assert ['integrations/dsh'] == ['web','integrations/dsh']), which is the fix landing.
no_tests.summary_claim: NOT DELIVERED. The commit message and the brief say `no_tests` is stated in the node section's summary line. Measured through the real entry on that same fixture: node['no_tests'] == ['integrations/dsh'] while node['summary'] == '2 of 2 node project(s) measured' and report['summary'] carries only pytest output. Nothing in aitelier/, core/ or api/ reads node['no_tests'] either.

shipped_bug_reproduced_as_mutant.plant: both halves of the shipped bug: `"checks": {f"{r['dir']}:{name}": check` back to `dict(check, dir=r['dir'])`, and `_node_ran_checks` back to the fold that rebuilt f"{chk.get('dir')}:{name}" and then prefixed node['dir'] again

other_mutants.plant: `_ran_no_tests` made install-agnostic again (return True instead of requiring a passing install)
`_node_ran_checks` stops prefixing the single-project report's bare keys with its dir
other_mutants.result: 1 failed, 22 passed - test_ran_checks_name_the_pairs_the_entry_itself_wrote (the author's shape test). The end-to-end probe stays green: a single-project repository's baseline keys are bare, so they are answered by node_gate_ran and that half of the helper is not reachable as behaviour - it is pinned as shape only.

probe_still_bites.restored: impl.py 0c10d1cc -> plant -> 0c10d1cc verified after every mutant ('pristine'); tree clean

changed_assertions_verdict.verdict: honest - neither change weakened what the probe can catch, and both new forms are stricter than what they replaced
changed_assertions_verdict.diff_scope: the whole file differs from mine in exactly two hunks (verified with diff against my committed probe), so nothing else was loosened while I was not looking; my untouched probe's independent run agrees (8 of 10 outcomes identical, and the 2 that differ are the 2 that were changed)
changed_assertions_verdict.assertion_1_no_tests_beside_a_failed_ins: mine asserted `node['no_tests'] == ['web','integrations/dsh']` - it pinned the DEFECT. Theirs asserts `== ['integrations/dsh']`. That is not a weaker test: it still requires the passing script-less project to be named in the very run where another project's install failed, and it now fails if the install-agnostic rule returns (measured: mutant Y). Honest, and cited in the commit message rather than done silently.
changed_assertions_verdict.assertion_2_diagnosis_test: mine asserted the broken shape (`'web:web:test' in node_ran`, `('node:web:test', False) in asked`) - a diagnosis of a world that no longer exists, so it had to be converted, not dropped. Theirs asserts the same detector from the healthy side: no token with more than one colon (catches the exact corruption), `'web:test' in node_ran`, and `('node:web:test', True) in asked` (the entry's tokens and the baseline's questions agree). Measured: it reddens on the shipped bug (mutant X). Nothing was lost; the renaming from `test_PROBE_diagnosis_*` to `test_the_real_entry_names_checks_the_way_the_baseline_asks_for_them` also stops it reading as a throwaway.

still_open: `no_tests` still reaches no reader, and the fix commit says otherwise: node['summary'] == '2 of 2 node project(s) measured' on a run whose node['no_tests'] == ['integrations/dsh'] (measured through run_tests). Either implement the summary sentence or correct the commit message and the node's own record - a stated-closed finding that is not in the code is worse than an open one.

A single-project repository still gets no `no_tests` at all: one project, no scripts, install passes -> node.checks == {'install'}, passed true, summary '1 of 1 ...', no key. `_ran_no_tests` is only consulted by `_aggregate_node_projects`. The adopted probe now PINS this as expected behaviour (test_PROBE_single_project_report_shape_is_unchanged asserts `'no_tests' not in report['node']`), so the gap is frozen rather than left open - worth a deliberate decision.

Housekeeping in the fix commit: `tests/unit/test_probe_review.py` was committed as a 0-byte file, and the adopted file still carries my header 'NON-AUTHOR REVIEW PROBE (transient, deleted before the report is committed)' and `test_PROBE_`-prefixed names, which now reads as a throwaway rather than the standing witness it is.

Unchanged and still parking: `configs/coding_impl.yaml`'s `test_evidence` requires `node.skipped: false`, so a mixed run (one project measurable, one not) is rejected by the shipped schema and ends at `test_evidence_missing`. The adopted probe still asserts that rejection and passes, so the behaviour is pinned, not fixed.

The single-project half of `_node_ran_checks` is pinned only as a shape (see mutant Z); no end-to-end behaviour depends on it today. Fine as it stands, but it is a pin on the token and not on an outcome.
